docs.title: Run Local AI Models Right Inside Go
docs.text:
litertlm-go brings Google's LiteRT-LM inference runtime straight into your Go applications — streaming text, vision and audio understanding, multimodal embeddings, typed Go tool calling, and structured JSON with no sidecar server.

Get Started in 5 Minutes Follow a Tutorial Browse 48 Examples

docs.title: See It in 15 Lines
docs.text:
Choose the workflow that fits what you are building. Each snippet runs in-process and can fetch its native library and model automatically on first run.

QuickstartVision Q&ATyped JSONEmbeddings 
ctx := context.Background()

libDir, err := litertlm.FetchLib(ctx, runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH, "v0.19.1")
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }

modelPath, err := litertlm.FetchModel(ctx, "litert-community/gemma3-1b-it-int4")
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }

client, err := litertlm.New(ctx, litertlm.WithLib(libDir), litertlm.WithModel(modelPath))
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
defer client.Close()

for chunk, err := range client.GenerateStream(ctx, "Write a haiku about local AI.") {
    if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
    fmt.Print(chunk.Text)
}

client, err := litertlm.New(ctx,
    litertlm.WithLib(libDir),
    litertlm.WithModel(visionModelPath),
    litertlm.WithVisionBackend("cpu"),
    litertlm.WithMaxTokens(4096),
)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
defer client.Close()

img, err := litertlm.ImageFromFile("scene.png")
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }

answer, err := client.GenerateMulti(ctx, []litertlm.Part{
    img,
    litertlm.Text("List the objects on the table."),
})

type Recipe struct {
    Title       string   `json:"title"`
    Ingredients []string `json:"ingredients"`
    Steps       []string `json:"steps"`
}

recipe, err := litertlm.GenerateData[Recipe](ctx, client,
    "Share a quick sourdough pancake recipe.",
    litertlm.WithRetries(2),
)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }

fmt.Println(recipe.Title, recipe.Ingredients)

embedder, err := litertlm.NewEmbeddingClient(ctx,
    litertlm.WithLib(libDir),
    litertlm.WithModel(embedModelPath),
)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
defer embedder.Close()

vec, err := embedder.Embed(ctx, "task: search query | text: parked cars",
    litertlm.WithNormalize(true),
    litertlm.WithOutputSize(256), // Matryoshka slice
)

docs.title: What You Can Build
docs.text:
Explore the full surface of litertlm-go, from one-line generation up to direct control of KV caches and model sections.

  • Zero-Hassle Provisioning & Delta Sync

    Download prebuilt LiteRT-LM shared libraries (FetchLib), stream .litertlm models from Hugging Face (FetchModel), and reuse unchanged sections on updates (PlanModelSync, SyncModelCache, C API 1.1+).

    Getting started

  • Stateful Multi-Turn Chat

    Keep conversation history cleanly with system prompts, custom prompt templates, transcript seeding (WithInitialMessages), thinking budgets, and O(1) conversation branching (Chat.Clone).

    Chat guide

  • Vision & Audio Multimodal

    Combine Text, ImageFromFile, and AudioFromFile parts in one-shot GenerateMulti calls or multi-turn Chat.SendMulti sessions with vision token budgets.

    Multimodal inputs

  • Multimodal Embeddings & Search

    Vectorize text, images, and audio in one shared embedding space using EmbeddingClient, batch processing, overflow chunking, and Matryoshka dimension truncation.

    Embeddings guide

  • Typed Go Tool Calling

    Reflect Go structs into JSON Schemas with RegisterTool, auto-dispatch multi-hop tool calls sequentially or concurrently, recover on transient tool errors, and enforce ToolChoice policies (1.1+).

    Tools guide

  • Structured JSON & Grammar Decoding

    Populate typed Go structs with GenerateData[T] and GenerateDataMulti[T], or enforce decode-time JSON Schema and regex constraints (WithConstraint) with logit penalties.

    Structured output

  • Hardware Acceleration & Diagnostics

    Inspect .litertlm capabilities without booting an engine (InspectModel), tune CPU (XNNPACK / YNNPACK) or GPU (Metal / WebGPU / D3D12), enable speculative decoding, and capture AI Edge Debugger traces (1.1+).

    Models & scaling

  • Direct Low-Level Engine Control

    Drop down to Engine, Session, and Conversation handles for explicit RunPrefill / RunDecode, KV-cache checkpoints (SaveCheckpoint / RewindToCheckpoint), log-prob scoring, tokenization, and WithModelFD.

    Low-level API

docs.title: How It Fits Together
docs.text:
Your Go binary loads the official LiteRT-LM shared library dynamically in-process via purego and FFI—no C compiler toolchain at build time and no separate Python or HTTP model server at runtime.

flowchart LR
    App["Your Go Application"] --> HL["High-Level API: Client · Chat · EmbeddingClient · GenerateData"]
    App --> LL["Low-Level API: Engine · Session · Conversation Handles"]
    HL --> Bind["In-Process FFI Layer: purego + jupiterrider/ffi"]
    LL --> Bind
    Bind --> Lib["Official LiteRT-LM Shared Library: liblitert-lm (v0.19.1+)"]
    Lib --> HW["Hardware Backends: CPU (XNNPACK / YNNPACK) · GPU (Metal / WebGPU / D3D12) · NPU"]
    Lib --> Artifact["Local .litertlm Model Archive"]

docs.title: Chat
docs.text:
The Chat API runs multi-turn conversations with optional system prompt and tool calling. It wraps the C-side Conversation API, which applies the model's chat template (e.g. Gemma's <|turn>user … <turn|>) on every turn.

chat, err := client.NewChat(ctx,
    litertlm.WithSystemPrompt("You are a friendly assistant."),
)
defer chat.Close()

reply, err := chat.Send(ctx, "Hi, what is your name?")
fmt.Println(reply.Text())

reply, err = chat.Send(ctx, "Tell me a fun fact.")
fmt.Println(reply.Text())

Chat keeps dialogue history internally — successive Send calls have access to prior turns.

docs.title: Creating NewChat(ctx, opts...)
docs.text:
Open a Chat from a Client with Client.NewChat(ctx, opts...). Call Close() on the returned *Chat when done.

Chat configuration:

Option Effect WithSystemPrompt(s) The system instructions. Pass just the text — the library handles the message envelope automatically. WithTool(defs ...) Registers one or more tools the model can call. Mix hand-built (RawTool) and typed (ManagedTool) tools. WithInitialMessages(msgs) Pre-seeds the conversation history with prior turns (supports both text and multimodal parts). WithConstrainedDecoding(on) Enables constrained-decoding mode for schema/regex grammars or ToolChoice. WithConstraintProvider(provider) Selects the constraint grammar provider (ConstraintProviderLLGuidance or ConstraintProviderNone). WithPromptTemplate(tmpl) Overrides the model's default chat prompt template. WithThinking(cfg) Sets conversation-wide thinking mode and token budget (ThinkingConfig{Enabled, TokenBudget}). WithExtraContext(json) Adds optional extra context (in JSON format) to the conversation preface. WithFilterChannelContentFromKVCache(on) Excludes model reasoning-channel tokens from the KV cache to conserve cache space. WithMaxToolHops(n) Caps the auto-dispatch tool execution loop iterations (defaults to 5).

docs.title: Send(ctx, message) and Reply
docs.text:
Send issues a synchronous user-role message and returns a *Reply.

type Reply struct{ /* unexported */ }
func (r *Reply) Text() string         // concatenated text content parts
func (r *Reply) ToolCalls() []ToolCall // structured function-call requests
func (r *Reply) HasToolCalls() bool
func (r *Reply) Raw() string          // original C-side JSON, for debugging

docs.title: SendStream(ctx, message)
docs.text:
SendStream is the streaming variant of Send. It returns an iter.Seq2[Chunk, error] over the model's response chunks as they arrive.

for chunk, err := range chat.SendStream(ctx, message) {
    if err != nil { break }
    fmt.Print(chunk.Text)
}

docs.title: Multimodal turns: SendMulti and SendMultiStream
docs.text:
Send image and audio inputs through the same Chat handle as text turns. SendMulti accepts []Part instead of string; the underlying Conversation accumulates KV state across turns regardless of modality, so follow-up text turns can reference earlier multimodal content.

img, err := litertlm.ImageFromFile("photo.jpg")
// ...
reply, err := chat.SendMulti(ctx, []litertlm.Part{
    img,
    litertlm.Text("Describe this image in one sentence."),
})

// Follow-up text turn — same Chat, image embeddings still in KV cache:
reply, err = chat.Send(ctx, "What's the dominant color?")

SendMultiStream is the streaming sibling:

for chunk, err := range chat.SendMultiStream(ctx, parts) {
    if err != nil { break }
    fmt.Print(chunk.Text)
}

Requirements:

  • Image Parts require WithVisionBackend on the Client at New time. Audio Parts require WithAudioBackend. Calling SendMulti with the wrong backend (or no backend) surfaces a C-side conversation_create failure.
  • An empty []Part is rejected up front with litertlm: SendMulti: empty parts. Pass at least one Part.
  • Tool dispatch behaves identically to Send — the model can emit tool_call content in response to multimodal input, and SendMulti runs the auto-dispatch loop the same way.
  • A []Part containing only text Parts is equivalent to Send with the text concatenated; the multimodal path is only needed when at least one image / audio Part is present.

Contrast with Client.GenerateMulti / GenerateMultiStream / GenerateMultiResponse: those are one-shot calls that open a fresh Conversation, run one inference, and discard it. KV state does not persist between calls. Use Chat.SendMulti* when you want successive turns to share the same conversation state.

docs.title: Per-call options
docs.text:
All five Chat.Send* methods accept variadic RuntimeOption values applied to a single turn (and to every dispatch hop the turn triggers).

WithVisualTokenBudget(n) caps the vision tokens consumed by a SendMulti / SendMultiStream turn. Text-only turns ignore it. Effective on Gemma 4 vision-enabled models.

reply, err := chat.SendMulti(ctx, []litertlm.Part{img, litertlm.Text("...")},
    litertlm.WithVisualTokenBudget(512),
)

WithReturnToolRequests(true) bypasses the auto-dispatch loop on Send, SendMulti, and SendToolResult. The first reply containing tool calls is returned directly via Reply.ToolCalls() even when every call maps to a registered ManagedTool. Pair with Chat.SendToolResult to feed the result back. Streaming methods ignore this flag — SendStream / SendMultiStream always run the dispatch loop.

reply, err := chat.Send(ctx, "What's the weather in Paris?",
    litertlm.WithReturnToolRequests(true),
)
for _, call := range reply.ToolCalls() {
    // inspect call.Function.Name / Arguments before dispatching manually
}

WithMaxConcurrentTools(n) runs tool handlers in parallel within a single dispatch hop. n <= 1 keeps the default sequential dispatch; n > 1 caps in-flight handlers at n. Result ordering in the follow-up tool-role message matches the model's original call order regardless of completion order. The first handler to fail (in real time) terminates the batch; sibling handlers see ctx cancellation and may bail.

reply, err := chat.Send(ctx, "Compare weather in Paris and Tokyo",
    litertlm.WithMaxConcurrentTools(4),
)

Tool handlers must be safe to invoke from multiple goroutines when n > 1. Shared mutable state in a closure-captured ManagedTool handler needs its own synchronization.

WithMaxOutputTokens(n) caps output tokens produced for this turn.

reply, err := chat.Send(ctx, "Write a long story",
    litertlm.WithMaxOutputTokens(50),
)

WithTurnThinking(cfg) toggles reasoning or adjusts the thinking token budget on a single turn. Pass TokenBudget: 0 to keep the C-side unlimited (-1) default, or pass a positive budget:

reply, err := chat.Send(ctx, "Compare merge sort and quicksort.",
    litertlm.WithTurnThinking(litertlm.ThinkingConfig{Enabled: true, TokenBudget: 256}),
)

See examples/thinking/.

WithConstraint(typ, pattern) enforces a ConstraintJSONSchema or ConstraintRegex grammar for a single turn. Open the chat with WithConstrainedDecoding(true) (and optionally WithConstraintProvider(ConstraintProviderLLGuidance)):

chat, err := client.NewChat(ctx,
    litertlm.WithConstrainedDecoding(true),
    litertlm.WithConstraintProvider(litertlm.ConstraintProviderLLGuidance),
)
reply, err := chat.Send(ctx, "Return Ada Lovelace's birth year as JSON.",
    litertlm.WithConstraint(litertlm.ConstraintJSONSchema, `{"type":"object","properties":{"year":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["year"]}`),
)

Constrained decoding requires a .litertlm model with embedded constraint-provider metadata. See examples/constrained-json/.

WithToolChoice(choice) enforces per-turn tool selection under constrained decoding (ToolChoiceAuto(), ToolChoiceNone(), ToolChoiceRequired(), ToolChoiceFunction(name), ToolChoiceAllowedTools(mode, names...), ToolChoiceRawJSON(raw)). Requires LiteRT-LM C API 1.1+; returns ErrUnimplemented on C API 1.0.0. See Tools → Controlling Tool Selection and examples/tool-choice/.

WithRepetitionPenalty(cfg), WithNoRepeatNgram(cfg), and WithSuppressTokens(tokenIDs...) adjust output logits per turn to curb loops or forbid specific token IDs:

reply, err := chat.Send(ctx, prompt,
    litertlm.WithRepetitionPenalty(litertlm.RepetitionPenaltyConfig{
        RepetitionPenalty: 1.15,
        PresencePenalty:   0.2,
        WindowSize:        64,
    }),
    litertlm.WithNoRepeatNgram(litertlm.NoRepeatNgramConfig{NgramSize: 4, WindowSize: 64}),
    litertlm.WithSuppressTokens(badTokenID),
)

See examples/logit-penalties/.

WithSampler is not per-call on Chat — configure the sampler with WithDefaultSampler on Client before opening the chat.

docs.title: Branching Conversations (Chat.Clone)
docs.text:
Use Chat.Clone() to fork an active conversation in O(1) without re-prefilling its system prompt, tool definitions, or earlier turns. Each cloned *Chat carries its own KV cache and can diverge independently; keep the parent *Chat open until all clones finish and call Close() on each clone:

chat, err := client.NewChat(ctx, litertlm.WithSystemPrompt("You are concise."))
defer chat.Close()

_, _ = chat.Send(ctx, "Context: Go was designed at Google in 2007.")

branch, err := chat.Clone()
if err != nil {
    return err
}
defer branch.Close()

r1, _ := chat.Send(ctx, "Who created Go?")
r2, _ := branch.Send(ctx, "What year did design start?")

See examples/clone/.

docs.title: Template Preface Rendering
docs.text:
To inspect the system prompts, initial message wrapper formatting, or tools schema structure exactly as they will be formatted for the model (before any user input is appended), call RenderPreface() on the underlying Conversation:

rendered, err := chat.Conversation().RenderPreface()
if err != nil {
    return err
}
fmt.Println(rendered)
// Output: <|im_start|>system\nYou are a helpful assistant...

docs.title: Tool calling
docs.text:
Two flavors of tool attach to a Chat via WithTool:

Flavor Constructor Dispatch RawTool NewRawTool Manual — Reply.ToolCalls() + Chat.SendToolResult ManagedTool RegisterTool Framework dispatches the typed handler

Both satisfy ToolDefinition and may be mixed in the same call:

chat, _ := client.NewChat(ctx,
    litertlm.WithSystemPrompt("You are a calculator. Always call the tool."),
    litertlm.WithTool(calcAdd),
)

When the chat has at least one ManagedTool registered, Chat.Send runs the dispatch loop and returns the post-tool natural-language reply directly. Replies whose tool calls aren't all dispatchable (unknown name or RawTool) come back for manual handling.

Cap the loop with WithMaxToolHops(n) (default 5). Override the per-tool error-propagation policy with WithToolPolicy(p) at RegisterTool time.

See the Tools guide for the full reference: schema reflection rules, dispatch semantics, mixed-registration behavior, ErrToolHopsExceeded / ToolHopsError, and ToolPolicy modes.

docs.title: ToolDefinition and ToolCall types
docs.text:
type ToolDefinition interface {
    Name() string
    Description() string
    Parameters() map[string]any  // JSON-Schema-shaped
}

type ToolCall struct {
    Type     string
    Function ToolCallFunction
}

type ToolCallFunction struct {
    Name      string
    Arguments map[string]any  // numbers come as float64 (encoding/json default)
}

docs.title: Multi-turn
docs.text:
A single Chat instance preserves history across calls. Successive Send calls let the model see prior turns:

chat.Send(ctx, "I'm planning a trip to Tokyo.")
chat.Send(ctx, "Suggest a 3-day itinerary.")  // model knows "Tokyo"
chat.Send(ctx, "What about the third day?")   // model knows the prior itinerary

When you need a fresh context, open a new Chat.

Seeding history with WithInitialMessages accepts both text-only and multimodal turns:

img, _ := litertlm.ImageFromFile("photo.jpg")
chat, _ := client.NewChat(ctx,
    litertlm.WithInitialMessages([]litertlm.Message{
        {Role: "user", Parts: []litertlm.Part{img, litertlm.Text("What is this?")}},
        {Role: "assistant", Parts: []litertlm.Part{litertlm.Text("A wooden table with a lamp.")}},
    }),
)
chat.Send(ctx, "What's the dominant color?")  // resumes with image in KV

docs.title: Introspection
docs.text:
Chat.TokenCount() returns the number of tokens currently held in the underlying conversation's KV cache (prefill + decode), accumulated across every turn — including tool-dispatch hops. Use it to project a chat against the engine's max-token budget.

n, err := chat.TokenCount() // tokens in the KV cache

It does not require WithBenchmarkEnabled. For a per-turn prefill / decode breakdown and reported KV-cache capacity (MaxNumTokens), read Conversation.BenchmarkInfo() instead (requires WithBenchmarkEnabled()).

docs.title: Client
docs.text:
The Client type is the high-level entry point to the LiteRT-LM runtime. Always pair New with defer client.Close() to release the underlying engine handles.

client, err := litertlm.New(ctx,
    litertlm.WithLib("/abs/path/to/dist/lib"),
    litertlm.WithModel("/abs/path/to/model.litertlm"),
    litertlm.WithBackend("cpu"),
    litertlm.WithMaxTokens(4096),
)
defer client.Close()

docs.title: Initializing the Client
docs.text:
Use litertlm.New to initialize a new client. The client automatically manages the underlying inference engine and configuration settings for you. Always pair it with a deferred close to ensure resources are properly released when your application exits:

client, err := litertlm.New(ctx, opts...)
defer client.Close()

docs.title: Construction options
docs.text: Use functional options to specify environment and inference engine settings.

docs.title: Library and model
docs.text: Option Effect WithLib(dir) Directory holding litert-lm.* (or legacy liblitertlm_c*.*). Empty → $LITERTLM_LIB. WithLibName(name) Override main shared library short-name (default "litert-lm"). Empty → $LITERTLM_LIB_NAME. WithModel(path) Path to a .litertlm file. Empty → $LITERTLM_MODEL. WithModelFD(fd) Raw file descriptor of the model file (unsupported on Windows). WithBackend(b) "cpu" (default), "gpu" ("apple" / "metal" normalize to "gpu"), or "ynnpack" (sets CPU + enables YNNPACK delegation when WithYNNPACK is unset). WithVisionBackend(b) Optional extra backend for vision inputs. WithAudioBackend(b) Optional extra backend for audio inputs.

docs.title: Engine settings
docs.text: Option Effect WithMaxTokens(n) Total token budget (prompt + output). Default 4096. WithCacheDir(dir) Engine artefact cache. Propagated to vision and audio executors. WithActivationDataType(t) 0=F32, 1=F16, 2=I16, 3=I8. WithPrefillChunkSize(n) CPU-backend prefill chunk size for dynamic models. WithSpeculativeDecoding(cfg) Configure SpeculativeDecodingConfig{Mode, Lenience} (SpeculativeDecodingOff, SpeculativeDecodingOn, SpeculativeDecodingAdaptive). Nonzero Lenience requires a runtime exporting litert_lm_speculative_decoding_config_set_lenience. WithSpeculativeDecodingEnabled(on) Boolean toggle for multi-token speculative decoding (ignored when WithSpeculativeDecoding is set). See examples/speculative/. WithBenchmarkEnabled() Turn on benchmark collection. Read per-call metrics via Response.Benchmark(). WithParallelSectionLoading(on) Parallel deserialization of .litertlm container sections. Defaults to true. WithYNNPACK(on) Enable YNNPACK CPU delegation before XNNPACK. WithMaxVisionTokensPerImage(n) Cap vision tokens generated per image. WithMaxImages(n) Cap image inputs per call on legacy backends. WithMetalResidencySet(on) Enable Metal residency sets on Apple GPU backends. WithGPUDecodeStepsPerSync(n) Configure decode steps between GPU synchronizations. WithGPUWaitForWeightUploads(on) Wait for weight uploads to complete during GPU initialization. WithRingbuffersLocalAttention(on) Store local attention KV caches in ringbuffers. WithSingleThreadedExecution(on) Run session execution on caller-driven threads rather than background workers. WithDebuggerEnabled(on) Enable AI Edge Debugger trace captures under a writable WithCacheDir (requires C API 1.1+; returns ErrUnimplemented on 1.0.0). WithSelectedSignatures(signatures...) Restrict the main executor to named model signatures (requires C API 1.1+; returns ErrUnimplemented on 1.0.0). WithDispatchLibDir(dir) LiteRT dispatch library directory for the NPU backend. WithVisionDispatchLibDir(dir) LiteRT dispatch library directory for vision NPU embedding backends. WithAudioDispatchLibDir(dir) LiteRT dispatch library directory for audio NPU embedding backends. WithMaxInputLength(n) Maximum text encoder sequence length for embedding engines. WithMinInputLength(n) Minimum text encoder sequence length for embedding engines. WithNumThreads(n) Set the number of threads for the CPU backend. WithAudioNumThreads(n) Set the number of threads for the audio CPU backend. WithLoRARank(rank) Set the startup LoRA rank for the engine. WithSupportedLoRARanks(ranks) Set the supported startup LoRA ranks for the engine. WithAudioLoRARank(rank) Set the startup audio LoRA rank for the engine. WithSupportedAudioLoRARanks(ranks) Set the supported startup audio LoRA ranks for the engine. WithConfigFile(path, profile) Load engine and sampler settings from a centralized config.json profile file.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Option Effect SetMinLogLevel(lvl) Package-level function (not a Client option). LogVerbose / LogDebug / LogInfo / LogWarning / LogError / LogFatal / LogQuiet. Call before New to override the C-side default of LogInfo.

docs.title: Sampler defaults
docs.text: Option Effect WithDefaultSampler(p) Sampler used for every Generate unless overridden per-call by WithSampler.

docs.title: Centralized configuration (WithConfigFile)
docs.text:
Store engine, speculative decoding, acceleration, thread-count, LoRA, and default sampler settings in a JSON file with a "default" block and per-model overrides under "models". Load a profile with litertlm.WithConfigFile("config.json", "model-profile"); explicit Go options applied after WithConfigFile override profile fields.

Supported keys inside each model entry include: backend, max_tokens, cache_dir, speculative_decoding_enabled, speculative_decoding_mode ("off" | "on" | "adaptive"), speculative_decoding_lenience, parallel_section_loading, enable_ynnpack, max_vision_tokens_per_image, metal_residency_set, gpu_decode_steps_per_sync, gpu_wait_for_weight_uploads, use_ringbuffers_local_attention, single_threaded_execution, enable_debugger, selected_signatures, num_threads, audio_num_threads, vision_dispatch_lib_dir, audio_dispatch_lib_dir, max_input_length, min_input_length, lora_rank, supported_lora_ranks, audio_lora_rank, supported_audio_lora_ranks, sampler_type ("top_k" | "top_p" | "greedy"), temperature, top_k, top_p, seed, lib_path, lib_name, and model_path.

See examples/config-file/.

docs.title: Model capabilities, runtime version, and errors
docs.text:
Query a .litertlm file's capabilities without initializing an engine using litertlm.InspectModel(path), or query the client's backing model with client.Capabilities() (when loaded by file path):

caps, err := client.Capabilities()
if err != nil {
    return err
}
fmt.Printf("type=%s ctx=%d dynamic=%v modalities=%v thinking=%v tools=%v\n",
    caps.ModelType, caps.MaxContextTokens, caps.IsDynamicContext,
    caps.SupportedModalities, caps.SupportsThinking, caps.SupportsFunctionCalling)

ModelCapabilities reports ModelType (ModelTypeLLM / ModelTypeEmbedding), MinRuntimeVersion, MaxContextTokens, IsDynamicContext, VisionSignatureLengths, EmbeddingDimension, EmbeddingSignatureLengths, per-modality hardware support (ModalityBackends, ModalityNPUBrand, ModalitySoCName), and convenience predicates (SupportsText(), SupportsVision(), SupportsAudio(), SupportsVideo()). See examples/capabilities/.

Inspect the loaded C API version at runtime with litertlm.APIVersion(). Native runtime failures return a *litertlm.CError carrying the failing Op, canonical StatusCode, and thread-local C++ diagnostic Message. Match conditions portably with errors.Is against sentinel errors (ErrCancelled, ErrInvalidArgument, ErrNotFound, ErrResourceExhausted, ErrFailedPrecondition, ErrUnimplemented, ErrInternal, etc.) or extract details via errors.As.

docs.title: Runtime Residency & Debugger Diagnostics
docs.text:
Adjust Metal GPU weight residency at runtime with client.SetMetalResidency(enable) (active on Apple Metal GPU backends; safely ignored on other platforms or CPU execution). See examples/metal-residency/.

When WithDebuggerEnabled(true) is paired with a writable WithCacheDir on C API 1.1+, query relative capture directories using chat.DebugCaptureDir() or session.DebugCaptureDir(). Captures contain unencrypted prompt/decoded text and activation tensors; remove capture directories manually after diagnostics. See examples/debugger/.

docs.title: Generate(ctx, prompt, opts...)
docs.text:
Synchronous one-shot inference. Returns the first candidate's text.

Per-call options are RuntimeOption values, shared with GenerateData and Chat.Send*:

Option Effect WithMaxOutputTokens(n) Cap output tokens for this call. WithSampler(p) Override the Client's default sampler. WithTurnThinking(cfg) Override thinking mode and token budget for the call. WithConstraint(typ, pattern) Apply a ConstraintRegex or ConstraintJSONSchema grammar. WithRepetitionPenalty(cfg) Apply repetition, presence, and frequency penalties. WithNoRepeatNgram(cfg) Ban repeating token n-grams within a history window. WithSuppressTokens(ids...) Ban listed token IDs from being sampled. 
text, err := client.Generate(ctx, "The capital of France is")

ctx cancellation is propagated to Conversation.Cancel internally, so context.WithTimeout and context.WithCancel apply:

ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
defer cancel()

text, err := client.Generate(ctx, prompt)
if errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
    // Model didn't finish in time.
}

docs.title: GenerateStream(ctx, prompt, opts...)
docs.text:
Provides access to token-by-token streaming.

for chunk, err := range client.GenerateStream(ctx, prompt) {
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    fmt.Print(chunk.Text)
    if chunk.Final {
        fmt.Println()
    }
}

Chunk is a value type:

type Chunk struct {
    Text  string
    Final bool
}

docs.title: GenerateResponse(ctx, prompt, opts...)
docs.text:
Use GenerateResponse when you need candidate metadata or per-call benchmark metrics alongside the text. It returns a *Response object:

resp, err := client.GenerateResponse(ctx, prompt)
if err != nil { return err }

fmt.Println(resp.Text())          // Generated reply text
fmt.Println(resp.NumCandidates()) // Number of candidates present (1 when non-empty)
if b := resp.Benchmark(); b != nil && len(b.DecodeTokensPerSec) > 0 {
    fmt.Printf("kv_cap=%d decode=%.1f tok/s\n", b.MaxNumTokens, b.DecodeTokensPerSec[0])
}

For log-probability candidate scoring or per-token scores and lengths, use Session.ScoreTexts with low-level Responses.Score and Responses.TokenLength (see Low-level API).

docs.title: Multimodal inputs
docs.text:
When the model supports vision or audio (and WithVisionBackend / WithAudioBackend are set), use the *Multi methods. They take a []litertlm.Part instead of a string prompt; everything else (opts, streaming, cancellation, response shape) is identical.

Method Returns GenerateMulti (string, error) GenerateMultiStream iter.Seq2[Chunk, error] GenerateMultiResponse (*Response, error)

These are one-shot: each call opens a fresh Conversation, runs one inference, and discards it. KV state does not persist between calls. For successive multimodal turns that share conversation state, use Chat.SendMulti / Chat.SendMultiStream (see Chat).

docs.title: Building Parts
docs.text: Constructor Purpose Text(s) Text prompt segment. Image(b) Image bytes (no MIME claimed). ImageWithMIME(b, "image/jpeg") Explicit MIME (jpeg / png / webp / gif / bmp). ImageFromFile(path) Read file; MIME from extension. Audio(b) / AudioWithMIME(b, mime) / AudioFromFile(path) Audio analogues.

docs.title: Example — vision Q&A
docs.text:
img, err := litertlm.ImageFromFile("/path/to/photo.jpg")
if err != nil { return err }

text, err := client.GenerateMulti(ctx, []litertlm.Part{
    img,
    litertlm.Text("What objects are visible?"),
})

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
EmbeddingClient provides a high-level API for generating dense vector embeddings from text and multimodal inputs using standalone .litertlm embedding models (ModelTypeEmbedding). Use litertlm.NewEmbeddingClient when your workflow needs semantic search, clustering, retrieval, or multimodal similarity without initializing a generative chat engine.

client, err := litertlm.NewEmbeddingClient(ctx,
    litertlm.WithLib("/abs/path/to/dist/lib"),
    litertlm.WithModel("/abs/path/to/embedding-model.litertlm"),
    litertlm.WithBackend("cpu"),
)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
defer client.Close()

vec, err := client.Embed(ctx, "Go concurrency with goroutines and channels",
    litertlm.WithNormalize(true),
    litertlm.WithOverflowStrategy(litertlm.OverflowChunkAndAverage),
)

docs.title: Initializing NewEmbeddingClient(ctx, opts...)
docs.text:
NewEmbeddingClient shares the same Option constructors as litertlm.New. Environment fallbacks $LITERTLM_LIB, $LITERTLM_LIB_NAME, and $LITERTLM_MODEL, along with WithConfigFile, apply in the same order. File-descriptor loading (WithModelFD) is not supported for embedding engines.

Embedding-specific construction options:

Option Effect WithNumThreads(n) Set CPU threads for text embedding execution. WithAudioNumThreads(n) Set CPU threads for audio embedding execution. WithCacheDir(dir) Share a compiled model cache across main, vision, and audio executors. WithVisionDispatchLibDir(dir) Specify the LiteRT dispatch library directory for vision NPU backends. WithAudioDispatchLibDir(dir) Specify the LiteRT dispatch library directory for audio NPU backends. WithMaxInputLength(n) Cap text encoder signature length (non-positive unsets). WithMinInputLength(n) Set minimum text encoder signature length (negative unsets). WithMaxVisionTokensPerImage(n) Set target vision tokens per image on embedding engines. WithActivationDataType(t) Select activation precision (0=F32, 1=F16, 2=I16, 3=I8).

Verify model type and native output dimensions before loading with litertlm.InspectModel or client.Capabilities():

caps, err := litertlm.InspectModel(modelPath)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
if caps.ModelType != litertlm.ModelTypeEmbedding {
    return fmt.Errorf("expected embedding model, got %s", caps.ModelType)
}
fmt.Printf("dim=%d signatures=%v\n", caps.EmbeddingDimension, caps.EmbeddingSignatureLengths)

docs.title: Generating Embeddings
docs.text:
Use Embed for single strings, EmbedBatch to vectorize multiple strings in one native batch call, or EmbedMulti / EmbedMultiBatch when inputs include Image or Audio Part segments alongside text.

vecs, err := client.EmbedBatch(ctx, []string{
    "Go concurrency with goroutines and channels",
    "Lightweight concurrent execution in Go",
},
    litertlm.WithNormalize(true),
    litertlm.WithOverflowStrategy(litertlm.OverflowChunkAndAverage),
)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
fmt.Printf("embedded %d vectors of length %d\n", len(vecs), len(vecs[0]))

Multimodal example combining image bytes and text:

img, err := litertlm.ImageFromFile("/path/to/photo.jpg")
if err != nil {
    return err
}

vec, err := client.EmbedMulti(ctx, []litertlm.Part{
    img,
    litertlm.Text("Sunset over the Pacific coastline"),
},
    litertlm.WithEmbeddingVisionTokensPerImage(280),
)

docs.title: Per-Call Options (EmbeddingOption)
docs.text:
Every Embed* method accepts variadic EmbeddingOption functions controlling normalization, special-token framing, long-input overflow handling, and Matryoshka truncation. When no options are passed, the runtime uses C defaults (normalize=true, insert_special_tokens=true, overflow=OverflowError).

Option Effect WithNormalize(on) Toggle L2 normalization on returned embedding vectors. WithInsertSpecialTokens(on) Toggle automatic BOS/EOS and modality marker insertion. WithOverflowStrategy(strategy) Select handling when input exceeds maximum signature length (OverflowChunkAndAverage, OverflowTruncate, OverflowError). WithOutputSize(n) Truncate vectors to the first n Matryoshka dimensions (n <= 0 keeps full model dimension). WithEmbeddingVisionTokensPerImage(n) Override vision tokens generated per image for a single request (n <= 0 unsets).

docs.title: Low-Level Control
docs.text: Drop down to EmbeddingEngineSettings, EmbeddingEngine, EmbeddingOptions, EmbeddingResponse, and EmbeddingResponses when you manage reusable EmbeddingOptions handles or InputData allocations directly across repeated calls. Access the underlying handles via client.Engine() and client.Settings(); see the Low-level API for handle lifetime rules.

docs.text:
Every example accepts the same discovery flags so you can switch seamlessly between automatic downloads and local paths on disk:

docs.title: Getting Started with litertlm-go
docs.text:
Prefer a guided walkthrough?

Follow Your First Local LLM App in 5 Minutes for a step-by-step tutorial with capability inspection and benchmarks, or jump straight to the Examples Gallery to browse all 48 runnable CLI programs.

litertlm-go supports two setup workflows: 1. Fully Programmatic Setup (Recommended): Automatically downloads and caches both the native C libraries and the model artifact in Go without manual setup steps. 2. Manual Provisioning: Manually download the .litertlm model file and native shared libraries, specifying their paths via environment variables or options.

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Go 1.26 or newer.
  2. Install the package: 
    go get github.com/vladimirvivien/litertlm-go@latest

docs.title: 2. Method 1: Fully Programmatic Setup (Recommended)
docs.text: In this workflow, Go automatically fetches the platform prebuilt libraries (litertlm.FetchLib) and downloads the .litertlm model from Hugging Face (litertlm.FetchModel):

docs.title: Go Program (main.go)
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"
    "runtime"

    "github.com/vladimirvivien/litertlm-go/pkg/litertlm"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    // 1. Automatically fetch and cache native LiteRT-LM shared libraries
    libDir, err := litertlm.FetchLib(ctx, runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH, "v0.19.1")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("FetchLib failed: %v", err)
    }

    // 2. Automatically download and cache the model from Hugging Face
    modelPath, err := litertlm.FetchModel(ctx, "litert-community/gemma3-1b-it-int4")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("FetchModel failed: %v", err)
    }

    // 3. Initialize the client using the staged library and model
    client, err := litertlm.New(ctx,
        litertlm.WithLib(libDir),
        litertlm.WithModel(modelPath),
    )
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("Client initialization failed: %v", err)
    }
    defer client.Close()

    // 4. Generate text
    text, err := client.Generate(ctx, "Write a haiku about the sea.")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("Generation failed: %v", err)
    }
    fmt.Println(text)
}

docs.title: Running the Program
docs.text: go run main.go

docs.title: 3. Method 2: Manual Model & Library Provisioning
docs.text: If you already have a model file and native shared libraries on disk:

docs.title: Step 1: Obtain the Model File
docs.text: Download a .litertlm model from Hugging Face's LiteRT Community (e.g., gemma3-1b-it-int4.litertlm or gemma-4-E2B-it.litertlm).

docs.title: Step 2: Obtain the Shared Libraries

Download the C-API release archive (litert_lm_c_api-1.0.0.zip) or macOS framework archive from LiteRT-LM Releases:

docs.title: Step 3: Go Program (main.go)
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "os"

    "github.com/vladimirvivien/litertlm-go/pkg/litertlm"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    client, err := litertlm.New(ctx,
        litertlm.WithLib(os.Getenv("LITERTLM_LIB")),
        litertlm.WithModel(os.Getenv("LITERTLM_MODEL")),
    )
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Printf("Initialization failed: %v\n", err)
        os.Exit(1)
    }
    defer client.Close()

    text, err := client.Generate(ctx, "Write a haiku about the sea.")
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Printf("Generation failed: %v\n", err)
        os.Exit(1)
    }
    fmt.Println(text)
}

docs.text:
Both methods produce text completions directly from the model:

Waves crash and secrets hold low,
Ocean breathes its peace now.

docs.title: 5. Inspecting Model Capabilities & Runtime Version
docs.text:
Before initializing a full inference engine, inspect a .litertlm artifact with litertlm.InspectModel to discover supported input modalities, thinking support, function calling, speculative decoding support, and default sampler settings without allocating KV caches or weights. You can also query the loaded runtime version with litertlm.APIVersion():

if err := litertlm.Load(os.Getenv("LITERTLM_LIB"), "cpu", ""); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
maj, min, pat, err := litertlm.APIVersion()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
caps, err := litertlm.InspectModel(os.Getenv("LITERTLM_MODEL"))
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Printf("C API %d.%d.%d | vision=%v audio=%v thinking=%v tools=%v spec=%v\n",
    maj, min, pat,
    caps.SupportsVision(), caps.SupportsAudio(),
    caps.SupportsThinking, caps.SupportsFunctionCalling, caps.SupportsSpeculativeDecoding,
)

See examples/capabilities/ for a runnable inspector program.

docs.title: Low-level API
docs.text:
litertlm-go exports every C-API symbol as a Go method providing fine-grained low-level control of the runtime engine.

Common reasons to drop down:

  • Manual prefill / decode & async streaming. Explicit RunPrefill / RunDecode or RunDecodeAsync / RunDecodeAsyncCh sequencing in place of Session.GenerateContent.
  • KV-cache checkpoints, rewinding & branching. Branch multiple continuations from one shared prompt with SaveCheckpoint, RewindToCheckpoint, RewindToStep, and Session.Clone / Conversation.Clone.
  • Per-turn constraint, thinking & penalty handles. Configure OptionalArgs with SetThinkingConfig, SetConstraint, SetRepetitionPenalty, SetNoRepeatNgram, SetSuppressTokens, and SetToolChoice (C API 1.1+).
  • Model capability inspection. Read .litertlm metadata (ModelType, MaxContextTokens, IsDynamicContext, ModalitySupportedBackends, NPU/SoC metadata, embedding dimensions) directly via OpenLoadedFile / LoadedFile without creating an engine.
  • Standalone embedding engines. Use EmbeddingEngineSettings, EmbeddingEngine, EmbeddingOptions, EmbeddingResponse, and EmbeddingResponses directly when reusing InputData buffers or option handles across calls.
  • Differential model sync (C API 1.1+). Drive NewModelSyncOptions, NewModelSyncPlanFromFile, ModelSyncUpdate, and ModelSyncCacheSync directly over a custom RangeFetcher or ModelSyncRangeWriter.
  • Runtime Metal residency & debugger captures. Toggle residency with Engine.SetMetalResidency, configure EngineSettings.SetEnableDebugger(true) (C API 1.1+), and inspect trace folders via Session.DebugInfo / Session.DebugCaptureDir and Conversation.SessionDebugInfo / Conversation.DebugCaptureDir.
  • Single-threaded execution. Drive caller-thread scheduling with SetSingleThreadedExecution(true) paired with Conversation.WaitUntilDone.
  • Text scoring. Session.ScoreTexts returns log-probabilities for candidate completions.
  • Token introspection. Engine.Tokenize / Engine.Detokenize, Engine.StartTokenIDs / StopTokenIDs.
  • Deterministic resource lifetimes. Explicit Delete() on each C-backed handle, with error checks via *CError.
  • Multimodal inputs. []InputData with NewBinaryInput(InputImage, …). For high-level multimodal calls, use Client.GenerateMulti / GenerateDataMulti[T] with Part constructors — see Client → Multimodal inputs.

docs.title: Resource lifetime management
docs.text:
The low-level API surfaces each C handle as a uintptr value type (Engine, Session, EngineSettings, SessionConfig, Conversation, ConversationConfig, OptionalArgs, Responses, BenchmarkInfo, JSONResponse, InputData, LoadedFile, EmbeddingEngine, EmbeddingEngineSettings, EmbeddingOptions, EmbeddingResponse, EmbeddingResponses, ModelSyncOptionsHandle, ModelSyncPlanHandle, ModelSyncResultHandle, SessionDebugInfo). Each provides a .Delete() method. ModelSyncRangeWriter is a borrowed handle valid only for the duration of a RangeFetcher callback and must not be retained. Low-level setters return error, wrapping C status failures in *CError with thread-local error messages and StatusCode sentinels.

Rules of thumb:

  • Every New*, OpenLoadedFile, Clone, ComputeEmbedding*, ModelSyncCacheSync, non-zero DebugInfo() / SessionDebugInfo(), and Generate* (when returning a handle) must be paired with defer h.Delete().
  • EmbeddingResponses.At(i) returns a borrowed EmbeddingResponse owned by the batch container; do not call Delete() on it.
  • A cloned Session or Conversation owns an independent handle, but keep parent resources (Engine, root Chat) alive for the lifetime of active clones.
  • Strings and embedding float slices returned by accessor methods are copied into Go memory, so they remain valid after the parent handle is deleted.

docs.title: Explicit prefill → decode
docs.text:
session, err := engine.NewSession(0)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
defer session.Delete()

in, err := litertlm.NewTextInputString("The capital of France is")
if err != nil {
    return err
}
defer in.Delete()

if err := session.RunPrefill([]litertlm.InputData{in}); err != nil {
    return err
}

resp, err := session.RunDecode()
if err != nil {
    return err
}
defer resp.Delete()

fmt.Println(resp.Text(0))

See examples/prefill-decode/.

docs.title: KV-cache checkpoints, rewinding, and cloning
docs.text:
Prefill a shared prefix once, save a named checkpoint or clone the session, then run async decoding across diverging branches:

shared, _ := litertlm.NewTextInputString("In a small seaside village,")
defer shared.Delete()
_ = session.RunPrefill([]litertlm.InputData{shared})
_ = session.SaveCheckpoint("after-prefix")

cloned, _ := session.Clone()
defer cloned.Delete()

for sc := range session.RunDecodeAsyncCh() {
    if sc.Err != nil { return sc.Err }
    fmt.Print(sc.Text)
}

_ = session.RewindToCheckpoint("after-prefix")
// RewindToStep(0) clears back to step 0 when resetting completely.
// Continue decoding on either session or cloned independently.

See examples/checkpoints/.

docs.title: Text scoring
docs.text:
Scoring advances model state; save a checkpoint before ScoreTexts and call RewindToCheckpoint afterward if the session will continue prefill or decode:

session, _ := engine.NewSession(0)
defer session.Delete()

in, _ := litertlm.NewTextInputString(prompt)
defer in.Delete()
_ = session.RunPrefill([]litertlm.InputData{in})
_ = session.SaveCheckpoint("before-score")

resp, _ := session.ScoreTexts([]string{" Paris."}, true)
defer resp.Delete()

score, _ := resp.Score(0)
length, _ := resp.TokenLength(0)
fmt.Printf("score=%v length=%d\n", score, length)

See examples/score/.

docs.title: Tokenize
docs.text:
tokens, _ := engine.Tokenize("Hello, world.")
roundTrip, _ := engine.Detokenize(tokens)
fmt.Println(tokens)
fmt.Println(roundTrip)

See examples/tokenize/.

docs.title: Supported Models & Scaling Guide
docs.text: litertlm-go supports .litertlm model artifacts produced for Google's LiteRT-LM runtime. This document outlines verified model families, parameter scaling requirements (from 1B up to 31B parameters), memory/VRAM allocation guidelines, and configuration options.

docs.title: 1. Verified Model Architectures (LiteRT-LM v0.19.1)
docs.text:
The test battery (pkg/litertlm/model_matrix_test.go) validates chat generation, tokenization round-trips, and streaming coherence across both CPU and GPU backends.

docs.title: Embedding Models (ModelTypeEmbedding)
docs.text:
Standalone embedding artifacts use litertlm.NewEmbeddingClient to generate dense vector representations for semantic retrieval and classification across text, vision, and audio. Verify model type and output dimensionality upfront via InspectModel.

Model Identifier Modalities Native Dimension Approximate Size litert-community/embeddinggemma-2-text-270m-litert-lm Text 768 ~165 MB litert-community/embeddinggemma-2-text-vision-440m-litert-lm Text, Vision 768 ~388 MB litert-community/embeddinggemma-2-740m-litert-lm Text, Vision, Audio 768 ~485 MB

See the Embeddings Guide and Tutorial: Local Multimodal Semantic Search & Zero-Shot Classification for runnable workflows.

docs.title: 2. Parameter Scaling & Memory Allocation Matrix
docs.text: Model memory consumption during inference consists of two primary components: 1. Static Weights Footprint: Base memory required to map and hold model parameters in memory. 2. Dynamic KV-Cache Footprint: Working memory allocated during prefill and decoding to hold key/value attention states for the active context window (maxNumTokens).

docs.title: 3. KV-Cache & Context Window Sizing
docs.text:
The dynamic memory allocated for the Key-Value (KV) cache scales linearly with sequence length:

Memory_KV = 2 × layers × kv_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_element × max_tokens

docs.title: Context Length Recommendations
docs.text:
• 2,048 – 4,096 tokens: Default for standard chat and single-document tasks. Leaves ample headroom on 8 GB / 16 GB host systems.
  • 8,192 – 16,384 tokens: Appropriate for document summarization and long multi-turn sessions. Ensure host system or GPU has at least 4 GB – 8 GB of memory headroom above base weight size.
  • Autosized Ringbuffers: On models configured with dynamic ringbuffers in config.json, the KV cache expands on-demand rather than pre-allocating the entire maxNumTokens window upfront.

docs.title: CPU Multi-Threading (WithNumThreads)
docs.text:
For models 7B and larger executing on the CPU backend, explicitly configure worker thread count to match physical CPU cores:

client, err := litertlm.New(ctx,
    litertlm.WithModel("gemma3-12b-it-int4.litertlm"),
    litertlm.WithBackend("cpu"),
    litertlm.WithNumThreads(runtime.NumCPU()),
)

docs.title: Prefill Chunking (WithPrefillChunkSize)
docs.text:
When processing long prompts on 12B–31B models on CPU, prefill chunking limits peak memory usage and keeps CPU cache locality high:

client, err := litertlm.New(ctx,
    litertlm.WithModel("gemma3-27b-it-int4.litertlm"),
    litertlm.WithBackend("cpu"),
    litertlm.WithPrefillChunkSize(512), // Process prompt in 512-token chunks
)

docs.title: Parallel File Loading (WithParallelSectionLoading)
docs.text:
For large model files (10 GB – 30 GB), enable parallel section loading to decrease model initialization time:

client, err := litertlm.New(ctx,
    litertlm.WithModel("qwen2.5-32b-int4.litertlm"),
    litertlm.WithParallelSectionLoading(true),
)

docs.title: Speculative Decoding (WithSpeculativeDecoding)
docs.text:
For models bundled with speculative decoding drafters (such as Gemma 4 E4B), configure multi-token draft speculation with SpeculativeDecodingOff, SpeculativeDecodingOn, or SpeculativeDecodingAdaptive:

client, err := litertlm.New(ctx,
    litertlm.WithModel("gemma-4-E4B-it.litertlm"),
    litertlm.WithSpeculativeDecoding(litertlm.SpeculativeDecodingConfig{
        Mode: litertlm.SpeculativeDecodingAdaptive,
    }),
)

Leave Lenience at 0 for lossless acceptance; nonzero Lenience values in (0, 1] require a native library exporting litert_lm_speculative_decoding_config_set_lenience. See examples/speculative/.

docs.title: YNNPACK & Ringbuffer Local Attention
docs.text: On supported CPU targets, enable YNNPACK delegation with WithYNNPACK(true) (or WithBackend("ynnpack")). For models supporting sliding-window/local-attention ringbuffers, pass WithRingbuffersLocalAttention(true) to store local attention KV state in ringbuffers.

docs.title: Capability Inspection (InspectModel)
docs.text: Query model support flags (SupportsSpeculativeDecoding, SupportsThinking, SupportsFunctionCalling, supported modalities, and default sampler fields) directly from .litertlm metadata with litertlm.InspectModel(path) before initializing an engine. See examples/capabilities/.

docs.title: GPU Buffer Sizing & Allocations
docs.text: On GPU backends using WebGPU / Direct3D 12, individual buffer allocations are subject to driver and API limits (typically ~2 GB per single buffer allocation). * Quantized int4 formats (e.g., Gemma 3 12B/27B int4) partition tensor weights into sub-buffers to stay within standard GPU driver limits. * If a model fails during initialization with failed to prepare engine, verify available dedicated VRAM or switch to the CPU backend (WithBackend("cpu")).

docs.title: 5. Automated Model Downloading (litertlm.FetchModel)
docs.text:
litertlm-go includes a built-in downloader to automatically download and stage .litertlm models from Hugging Face or direct URLs with progress reporting and range-based resumable transfers:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"

    "github.com/vladimirvivien/litertlm-go/pkg/litertlm"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    // Download Gemma 3 1B from Hugging Face with progress updates
    modelPath, err := litertlm.FetchModel(ctx, "litert-community/gemma3-1b-it-int4",
        litertlm.WithModelProgress(func(downloaded, total int64, pct float64) {
            if total > 0 {
                fmt.Printf("\rDownloading: %.1f%% (%.1f / %.1f MB)", pct, float64(downloaded)/1e6, float64(total)/1e6)
            }
        }),
    )
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("FetchModel failed: %v", err)
    }
    fmt.Printf("\nModel cached at: %s\n", modelPath)
}

Supported identifier formats: * Hugging Face Shorthand: litert-community/gemma3-1b-it-int4 or gemma3-1b-it-int4 * Full Repo + File: hf:google/gemma-3-1b-it:model.litertlm * Direct HTTPS URL: https://huggingface.co/litert-community/gemma3-1b-it-int4/resolve/main/gemma3-1b-it-int4.litertlm

docs.title: Differential Model Sync (C API 1.1+)
docs.text:
On runtimes supporting LiteRT-LM C API 1.1.0+, PlanModelSync, SyncModel, and SyncModelCache compare an existing local .litertlm container against a remote RangeFetcher (such as modelfetch.NewHTTPRangeFetcher) and download only modified sections:

fetcher := modelfetch.NewHTTPRangeFetcher(http.DefaultClient, "litert-community/gemma3-1b-it-int4")
plan, err := litertlm.PlanModelSync(ctx, localPath, fetcher,
    litertlm.WithFullDownloadThreshold(0.80),
)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
fmt.Printf("Up to date: %v | Download: %d B | Reuse: %d B\n",
    plan.UpToDate, plan.BytesToDownload, plan.BytesToReuse)

cachedPath, err := litertlm.SyncModelCache(ctx, cacheDir, "gemma3-1b-it-int4", fetcher,
    litertlm.WithOfflineFallback(true),
    litertlm.WithCheckDiskSpace(true),
)

Transport failures and HTTP timeouts map to StatusUnavailable and StatusDeadlineExceeded, enabling offline fallback to a valid cached artifact when WithOfflineFallback(true) is active. Calling ModelSync functions against a C API 1.0.0 (v0.19.1) library returns *CError wrapping ErrUnimplemented. See examples/model-sync/.

docs.title: 6. Integration Test Execution
docs.text:
To execute the model matrix battery against local model files:

# Set paths to staging directory and models directory
export LITERTLM_TEST_LIB="/path/to/litertlm/lib"
export LITERTLM_TEST_MODELS_DIR="/path/to/models"

# Run tests on CPU backend
go test -race -v -run TestModelMatrix ./pkg/litertlm

# Run tests on GPU backend
export LITERTLM_TEST_BACKEND="gpu"
go test -race -v -run TestModelMatrix ./pkg/litertlm

docs.title: Structured output
docs.text:
GenerateData[T] and GenerateDataMulti[T] produce a typed *T populated from the model's response, without manual JSON parsing in caller code.

type Recipe struct {
    Title       string   `json:"title"`
    Ingredients []string `json:"ingredients"`
    Steps       []string `json:"steps"`
}

recipe, err := litertlm.GenerateData[Recipe](ctx, client,
    "Recipe for chocolate chip cookies.",
    litertlm.WithRetries(2),
)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
fmt.Println(recipe.Title)
fmt.Println(recipe.Ingredients)

docs.title: Signatures
docs.text:
func GenerateData[T any](
    ctx context.Context,
    c *Client,
    prompt string,
    opts ...RuntimeOption,
) (*T, error)

func GenerateDataMulti[T any](
    ctx context.Context,
    c *Client,
    parts []Part,
    opts ...RuntimeOption,
) (*T, error)

T must be a struct or pointer-to-struct for the primary path. Other kinds (slices, scalars, maps) route through the fallback path described below.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: GenerateData uses a two-tier strategy to extract structured data from the model:

docs.title: 1. Primary Path: Synthesized Tool Calling
docs.text:
• Automatic Tool Creation: The library reflects on your Go struct T and automatically registers a temporary "capture tool" representing its schema.
  • Model Directive: It instructs the model to populate the fields of this tool to answer your prompt.
  • Direct Extraction: When the model calls the tool, the library captures the arguments directly and unmarshals them into your struct T. This path leverages the model's native function-calling capabilities.

docs.title: 2. Fallback Path: Prompt Engineering & Tolerant JSON Parsing
docs.text: If the model does not support tool calling, or if the tool call fails: * Schema Hinting: The library generates a compact JSON shape hint from your Go struct. * Prompt Augmentation: It instructs the model to return valid JSON matching that exact shape, with no markdown formatting or commentary. * Tolerant Parsing: The library cleans up the model's output (stripping markdown fences, preambles, and conversational prose), extracts the raw JSON block, and unmarshals it into your struct T.

docs.title: Retry semantics
docs.text:
WithRetries(n) controls iteration count: each attempt runs the primary path then the fallback path in sequence. The full pair counts as one attempt; up to 1+n attempts run before returning the last parse error.

Retries fire on parse-path failures. Generate-phase errors (ctx.Err(), FFI failures, model crashes) propagate immediately.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
GenerateData[T] and GenerateDataMulti[T] accept any RuntimeOption (forwarding sampling, thinking, and penalty options to the underlying turns):

Option Effect WithRetries(n) Max retry attempts on parse failure. Default 0 (one total attempt). WithSchemaInstruction(s) Override the fallback path's default preamble. s is a Printf format string with one %s. WithMaxOutputTokens(n) Cap output tokens on the fallback path. WithSampler(p) Override the Client's default sampler on the fallback path. WithTurnThinking(cfg) Override reasoning behavior and token budget for the generation call. WithRepetitionPenalty(cfg) Apply repetition/presence/frequency penalties during generation. WithNoRepeatNgram(cfg) Ban repeating n-grams during generation. WithSuppressTokens(ids...) Ban listed token IDs during generation.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
GenerateData returns a *GenerateDataError on failure. Use errors.As to distinguish phases.

recipe, err := litertlm.GenerateData[Recipe](ctx, client, prompt)
if err != nil {
    var gd *litertlm.GenerateDataError
    if errors.As(err, &gd) {
        switch gd.Phase {
        case "parse":
            log.Printf("model returned bad JSON after %d attempts:\n%s",
                gd.Attempts, gd.Raw)
        case "generate":
            log.Printf("model call itself failed: %v", gd.Err)
        }
    }
    return err
}

Type:

type GenerateDataError struct {
    Phase    string  // "generate" | "parse"
    Err      error   // wrapped underlying error
    Raw      string  // model output that failed to parse (parse phase)
    Attempts int     // 1-indexed
}

docs.title: Multimodal: GenerateDataMulti[T]
docs.text:
GenerateDataMulti[T] accepts a []Part carrying image, audio, and text segments. Requires a multimodal model.

img, err := litertlm.ImageFromFile("/path/to/recipe-card.jpg")
if err != nil { return err }

recipe, err := litertlm.GenerateDataMulti[Recipe](ctx, client,
    []litertlm.Part{
        img,
        litertlm.Text("Extract the recipe shown in the image."),
    },
    litertlm.WithRetries(2),
)

Placement rule for the tool-call directive (primary path) and the schema instruction (fallback path): both prepend to the LAST text Part in parts. When parts contains no text Part, a synthesized Text(...) is appended at the end. The caller's slice is never mutated.

GenerateData[T] is the text-only convenience over GenerateDataMulti[T].

docs.title: Grammar-constrained JSON (WithConstraint)
docs.text:
When working inside a Chat or Client.Generate call with a model that embeds constraint-provider metadata (such as Gemma 3 1B, Gemma 4 E2B, or Qwen 3 0.6B), you can enforce exact JSON Schema or regular-expression syntax at decode time instead of relying on post-generation parsing:

chat, err := client.NewChat(ctx,
    litertlm.WithConstrainedDecoding(true),
    litertlm.WithConstraintProvider(litertlm.ConstraintProviderLLGuidance),
)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
defer chat.Close()

reply, err := chat.Send(ctx, "Extract Ada Lovelace's name and age as JSON.",
    litertlm.WithConstraint(litertlm.ConstraintJSONSchema, `{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"age":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["name","age"]}`),
)

Models without embedded constraint-provider metadata fail NewChat with Failed to create GemmaModelConstraintProvider. For portable struct extraction across any model, use GenerateData[T]. See examples/constrained-json/.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Tools let the model trigger function calls — fetching weather, doing arithmetic, looking up records — and incorporate the results back into its reply. litertlm-go offers two flavors:

Flavor Constructor Dispatch RawTool NewRawTool Manual — Reply.ToolCalls() + Chat.SendToolResult ManagedTool RegisterTool Framework dispatches the typed handler

Both implement ToolDefinition and may be mixed in the same WithTool(...) call.

type ToolDefinition interface {
    Name() string
    Description() string
    Parameters() map[string]any
}

docs.title: RegisterTool — typed tools with auto-dispatch
docs.text:
RegisterTool reflects over the input struct to build a JSON-Schema parameters object, registers the tool on the Client so its name cannot be reused, and returns a *ManagedTool[I, O] ready to attach to chats with WithTool.

type WeatherInput struct {
    Location string `description:"city and state, e.g. 'Boston, MA'"`
}
type WeatherOutput struct {
    Forecast string `json:"forecast"`
}

weather, err := litertlm.RegisterTool(client, "get_weather",
    "Get a weather forecast for a US city",
    func(ctx context.Context, in WeatherInput) (WeatherOutput, error) {
        return WeatherOutput{Forecast: forecastFor(in.Location)}, nil
    })

docs.title: Schema reflection rules
docs.text:
When you register a Go function as a tool, the library automatically translates the input struct into a JSON Schema. The rules are simple:

  • Exported Fields: Only exported fields are included in the schema.
  • Names & Descriptions: Field names default to the Go field name (lowercased) or are customized using the json tag. You can add descriptions using the description tag.
  • Required vs. Optional: Non-pointer fields are required; pointer fields are optional.
  • Supported Types: Supports strings, booleans, integers, floats, slices, arrays, nested structs, and pointers.

The input type I must be a struct or a pointer-to-struct. Other types will return an error during registration.

docs.title: Generated schema shape
docs.text:
The resulting parameters map matches the OpenAI / Anthropic function-calling convention:

{
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "location": {"type": "string", "description": "city and state, e.g. 'Boston, MA'"}
    },
    "required": ["location"]
}

docs.title: NewRawTool — hand-built declarations
docs.text:
For declarations that don't fit the reflection rules (dynamic parameters, hand-crafted schemas, tools whose handlers live outside the chat lifecycle), construct the parameters map yourself:

search := litertlm.NewRawTool("search_web",
    "Search the public web",
    map[string]any{
        "type": "object",
        "properties": map[string]any{
            "query": map[string]any{"type": "string"},
        },
        "required": []string{"query"},
    })

RawTool carries a name, description, and parameters but no handler. The model can call it; the caller handles the call manually with Reply.ToolCalls() and Chat.SendToolResult.

docs.title: Attaching tools to a chat
docs.text:
WithTool is variadic and accepts any ToolDefinition:

chat, _ := client.NewChat(ctx,
    litertlm.WithSystemPrompt("..."),
    litertlm.WithTool(weather, search, calcAdd),
)
defer chat.Close()

Multiple WithTool(...) calls accumulate. Duplicate names error at NewChat time.

docs.title: Auto-dispatch loop
docs.text:
When the chat has at least one ManagedTool registered, Chat.Send runs a dispatch loop:

flowchart TD
    S["Send(user message)"] --> T["transport.SendMessage -> reply"]
    T --> Q1{"Reply has tool calls?"}
    Q1 -->|No| R["Return reply"]
    Q1 -->|Yes| Q2{"Every call dispatchable?"}
    Q2 -->|No| M["Return reply for manual handling"]
    Q2 -->|Yes| H["Invoke each ManagedTool handler"]
    H --> B["Bundle tool results and loop"]
    B --> T

A call is dispatchable when its name maps to a ManagedTool in the chat's registry. RawTool entries and unknown names are non-dispatchable; if any call in a reply is non-dispatchable, the loop returns the reply for the caller to handle the whole turn manually.

Chat.SendToolResult enters the same loop — the model's response to a tool result might trigger more calls, which the framework dispatches the same way.

docs.title: Per-call dispatch knobs
docs.text:
Three RuntimeOption values control dispatch on a per-Send* basis (see Chat → Per-call options for the full list):

  • WithMaxConcurrentTools(n) — when a reply contains multiple tool calls, dispatch handlers concurrently capped at n in-flight. n <= 1 (the default) is sequential. Result ordering in the follow-up tool-role message matches the model's call order regardless of completion order. Handlers must be safe to invoke from multiple goroutines when n > 1.
  • WithReturnToolRequests(true) — bypass dispatch entirely for the current Send / SendMulti / SendToolResult. The first reply carrying tool calls is returned via Reply.ToolCalls() for manual handling. Streaming methods ignore the flag.
  • WithMaxToolHops(n) — see below; applies at NewChat time, not per call.

docs.title: WithMaxToolHops(n) — cap iterations
docs.text:
Each iteration is one model→tool→model round-trip. The default cap is 5; override per chat:

chat, _ := client.NewChat(ctx,
    litertlm.WithTool(weather),
    litertlm.WithMaxToolHops(3),
)

Exceeding the cap returns an error matching errors.Is(err, ErrToolHopsExceeded). Use errors.As to a *ToolHopsError for the partial last reply:

reply, err := chat.Send(ctx, prompt)
if err != nil {
    var hops *litertlm.ToolHopsError
    if errors.As(err, &hops) {
        log.Printf("model still calling tools after %d hops", hops.Hops)
        log.Printf("last reply: %s", hops.LastReply.Raw())
    }
    return err
}

n <= 0 is ignored (default applies). The cap exists to bound a runaway model, not to disable dispatch — chats with no ManagedTool registered never enter the loop.

docs.title: ToolPolicy — error handling per tool
docs.text:
Each ManagedTool carries a ToolPolicy set with WithToolPolicy at registration time. The policy controls what happens when the handler returns an error during dispatch:

Policy Behavior ToolPolicyReturnOnError (default) Propagate the error from Chat.Send; loop ends. The model is not informed. ToolPolicyInformOnError Marshal {"error": "<err.Error()>"} as the tool's response and continue. The model can retry, apologize, or pick a different tool. 
// Default: a validation error stops the loop and surfaces to the caller.
validate, _ := litertlm.RegisterTool(client, "validate_input", "...",
    func(ctx context.Context, in ValidateInput) (Validated, error) {
        return doValidate(in)
    })

// Inform-on-error: transient failures the model can react to.
weather, _ := litertlm.RegisterTool(client, "get_weather", "...",
    func(ctx context.Context, in WeatherInput) (WeatherOutput, error) {
        return forecastFor(in.Location)
    },
    litertlm.WithToolPolicy(litertlm.ToolPolicyInformOnError))

Pick ToolPolicyReturnOnError for invariants the framework should defend (a corrupted state is a programmer bug; bubble it up). Pick ToolPolicyInformOnError for transient failures the model can reasonably handle conversationally (rate limits, retryable network errors, ambiguous queries the model might rephrase).

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
SendStream and SendMultiStream run the same dispatch loop as Send / SendMulti. Text chunks from each turn are yielded immediately; intermediate Final markers from inner turns are suppressed. The iterator emits one trailing synthetic Final chunk after the loop terminates. Replies whose tool calls include any non-dispatchable entry (a RawTool or an unknown name) end the stream with an error.

Streaming methods ignore WithReturnToolRequests — manual handling of tool calls requires a *Reply, so use Send for that flow.

docs.title: Controlling Tool Selection (WithToolChoice)
docs.text:
Per-turn tool choice constrains whether the model calls any tool, avoids calling tools, or calls a specific named function. Pass WithConstrainedDecoding(true) at NewChat time and pass WithToolChoice(...) on Chat.Send or Chat.SendStream:

Constructor Policy ToolChoiceAuto() Model decides whether to invoke a tool or respond with text. ToolChoiceNone() Prevents tool calls on the turn. ToolChoiceRequired() Forces at least one tool call from the registered tools. ToolChoiceFunction(name) Forces invocation of the named function. ToolChoiceAllowedTools(mode, names...) Restricts callable tools to names under "auto" or "required" mode. ToolChoiceRawJSON(rawJSON) Supplies an OpenAI tool_choice JSON payload verbatim. 
reply, err := chat.Send(ctx, "Check the weather in Boston.",
    litertlm.WithToolChoice(litertlm.ToolChoiceFunction("get_weather")),
)
if errors.Is(err, litertlm.ErrUnimplemented) {
    // Loaded LiteRT-LM library does not expose C API 1.1+ tool_choice.
}

WithToolChoice requires LiteRT-LM C API 1.1+; against C API 1.0.0, the call fails cleanly with a *CError wrapping ErrUnimplemented. See examples/tool-choice/.
